newsitem.title: ISRAEL: American gives Israel $30 mln for business school.
newsitem.headline: American gives Israel $30 mln for business school.

text.p: An American businessman has given an Israeli university $30 million to create the world's first business school devoted to managing high technology, the university's U.S. fundraising organisation said.
The money was donated to the Technion institute in Haifa by William Davidson, president and chief executive officer of Guardian Industries Corp which makes glass and glass products.

"Israel has a critical need for a world-class business school that will equip its technological pioneers with the skills necessary to translate successes in the laboratory into successes in the global marketplace," Davidson said in a statement.

The school will provide university graduates and executives who have scientific and engineering degrees with the management skills required by high technology, export-oriented businesses, the American Technion Society said.
The Technion, formally known as the Israel Institute of Technology, has 11,000 students studying science and engineering.
